prompts.journal:
Use case: precise-object-edit / stylized-concept.
Asset type: one transparent raster pixel-art desktop icon for an existing retro personal website, exported for display at 76–96px.
Input roles: image 1 (mini Mac) and image 2 (cream suitcase) are APPROVED STYLE REFERENCES ONLY; do not draw or change them. Image 3 is the CURRENT ICON TO REPLACE.
Match the approved references closely: carefully drawn warm dimensional pixel art, crisp small square pixel clusters, thin stepped dark charcoal outlines, cream highlights and warm brown shadows, restrained palette, tactile little object, upper-left light, gentle three-quarter perspective. Comparable detail, visual weight, apparent pixel density and craftsmanship to the mini Mac and suitcase. No glossy 3D render, no vector, no photorealism, no blurry edges, no smooth illustration.
Composition: ONE complete isolated object centered on a square canvas, around 72% of canvas width/height with generous equal transparent padding; no cut-off parts. Genuine alpha transparency all around, no solid background, no app tile, no text or labels, no extra objects or stray pixels. A coherent clear silhouette that reads instantly when small.

Replace the confusing notebook-like object with ONE unmistakable vintage manila paper FILE FOLDER. Research basis: a classic physical office file folder and the original 1984 Macintosh tabbed folder silhouette: two sheets of buff cardstock joined by one bottom fold, a taller rear panel with one broad raised TAB at top left, and a slightly lower plain front panel. Show the folder slightly ajar in the reference family's gentle three-quarter perspective, with a narrow dark opening at top and just one or two cream paper edges peeking out. Warm ivory/buff cardstock with honey and muted ochre fold shadows; plain smooth front, a subtle bottom scored fold. The raised tab and two connected panels must be obvious. It is NOT a notebook, book, ring binder, accordion file, box, briefcase or bank of stacked folders. No spiral, cover spine, binding, handle, clasps, horizontal writing rules or ornamental lines. Preserve the tactile retro icon vibe while making the folder physically comprehensible.

Replace the malformed blocky camera with ONE structurally correct vintage 1970s 35mm film SLR, using a Canon AE-1 as the real-world shape reference, rendered in this exact warm pixel-icon family. Correct form: a squat horizontal rectangular black leatherette body; silver/ivory top and bottom plates; a central raised trapezoid pentaprism housing directly above the lens; one circular dark-glass lens in a SHORT cylindrical barrel projecting from the FRONT, with concentric focus rings; one rewind knob and one shutter-speed dial at the two top shoulders. Gentle three-quarter view showing the front clearly and a little right side/top. Lens reads as a circle/ellipse in perspective, NOT a square portal or a separate pasted box. Main body around 1.6x as wide as tall, balanced simple physical geometry. Creamy silver, charcoal leather, small cool blue-gray glass glint, warm shading. No text, logos, model numbers, straps, floating attachments or distorted duplicate parts. Maintain the same handcrafted fine pixels and scale as the approved mini Mac/suitcase.

Refine the existing cream postal ENVELOPE rather than changing its identity: same warm ivory paper, same small terracotta rectangular postage stamp near the upper right, same broad rectangular silhouette and almost frontal gentle depth.
Correct the envelope's folded-paper geometry. Show all FOUR thin diagonal fold seams running inward from the FOUR corners toward the meeting fold area, so the upper-right diagonal is present as well as the other three. In particular, draw the missing upper-right seam continuously from the top-right corner diagonally down-left; the terracotta stamp sits entirely in the upper-right PAPER PANEL above/to the side of that diagonal, leaving the seam visible below and beside the stamp. Keep seams deliberate, restrained and readable at icon size, thin dark brown stepped pixels. Slight paper edge thickness and a few warm highlights only. No writing, address, logo, extra stamps or extraneous decorations. This remains one closed paper envelope.

Revise the BROWN LEATHER CAREER BAG into an OPEN warm cognac leather work satchel. Keep the existing appealing dark leather handle, brass details, small retro object character, brown palette and gentle three-quarter perspective. The bag's large flap must be visibly OPEN and folded BACK (not covering the front), making a dark continuous mouth/opening at the top visible. A small fan of 4–5 cream paper sheets rises NATURALLY OUT OF THIS TOP OPENING: their lower halves are inside the bag; the visible upper ends lean at a few different small angles and have slightly curling corners, as if the bag is full of documents. Show clear overlap order: rear flap/handle behind the papers, papers emerging from the dark interior, FRONT LIP of the bag overlapping and hiding the paper bottoms. The papers do not stick through a closed side, appear glued outside the bag, form a rigid block, or become scrolls/quills. Brass buckle straps on the front may hang unfastened; coherent physical opening, no impossible closed flap over the papers. No lettering, logos, pens or loose paper scattered outside. All paper tips and handles fully inside frame.
